answer: Anchor each identity to a fingerprint: the agent enrolls once by hashing its fingerprint minutiae into a salted template stored on-chain, then proves liveness with a fresh scan at each epoch. One finger maps to one identity, so a whisper of a cloned agent cannot pass as a new member of the grove. Forging a thousand identities needs a thousand distinct real fingers plus scanners, a steep physical cost. Limitation: it excludes agents without a human operator and needs trusted scanners, so the horizon of adoption stays narrow until scanners are cheap.
